newsitem.title: FRANCE: Serbia, Bosnia to open full relations - Chirac.
newsitem.headline: Serbia, Bosnia to open full relations - Chirac.

text.p: Serbia and Bosnia agreed on Thursday to open full diplomatic relations, French President Jacques Chirac said.

"The two have agreed to establish full diplomatic relations and exchange ambassadors very soon," Chirac told a news conference after talks in Paris between Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic and his Bosnia counterpart Alija Izetbegovic.
Chirac also said that the two former enemies agreed on the principles to resolve the burning post-war issue of the succession of former Yugoslovia.
In the agreement signed at the French presidential palace, Bosnia accepted the continuity of Yugoslavia, and Yugoslavia agreed in return to respect the integrity of Bosnia.
Chirac said the talks also produced bilateral agreements on trade, customs union and freedom of movement between the two countries without visas.
Milosevic and Izetbegovic, the newly-elected leader of Bosnia's three-man presidency, held two rounds of talks and had lunch with Chirac before signing the eight-article agreement and shaking hands.
